sanskrit: arjunas tu mahārāja śaraiḥ śaravighātibhiḥ vārayām āsa tān astāṃs tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: But Arjuna, O great king, with arrows that shattered other arrows warded off those shafts hurled at him; and it seemed a thing of wonder.

sanskrit: tataḥ punar atikruddho rājā prāgjyotiṣādhipaḥ preṣayām āsa nāgendraṃ balavac chvasanopamam
english: Then once more, exceedingly enraged, the king who ruled Prāgjyotiṣa sent forth a mighty lord of elephants, swift as the rushing wind.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ saṃprekṣya balavān pākaśāsaniḥ nārācam agnisaṃkāśaṃ prāhiṇod vāraṇaṃ prati
english: Seeing it bearing down upon him, the mighty son of the chastiser of Pāka loosed against the elephant an iron shaft that blazed like fire.

sanskrit: sa tena vāraṇo rājan marmaṇy abhihato bhṛśam papāta sahasā bhūmau vajrarugṇa ivācalaḥ
english: Struck hard by it in a vital part, O king, that elephant fell suddenly to the earth like a mountain shattered by the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: sa patañ śuśubhe nāgo dhanaṃjayaśarāhataḥ viśann iva mahāśailo mahīṃ vajraprapīḍitaḥ
english: As it fell, that elephant, smitten by Dhanaṃjaya's arrow, shone like a great mountain crushed by the thunderbolt sinking into the earth.

sanskrit: tasmin nipatite nāge vajradattasya pāṇḍavaḥ taṃ na bhetavyam ity āha tato bhūmigataṃ nṛpam
english: When that elephant of Vajradatta had fallen, the son of Pāṇḍu said to the king who had come down to the ground, "You need have no fear."

sanskrit: abravīd dhi mahātejāḥ prasthitaṃ māṃ yudhiṣṭhiraḥ rājānas te na hantavyā dhanaṃjaya kathaṃ cana
english: For the mighty-spirited Yudhiṣṭhira had said to me as I set out, "Those kings, Dhanaṃjaya, are by no means to be slain by you."

sanskrit: sarvam etan naravyāghra bhavatv etāvatā kṛtam yodhāś cāpi na hantavyā dhanaṃjaya raṇe tvayā
english: "Let all this be ended here, O tiger among men, with only this much done; nor, Dhanaṃjaya, are the warriors to be slain by you in battle."

sanskrit: vaktavyāś cāpi rājānaḥ sarvaiḥ saha suhṛjjanaiḥ yudhiṣṭhirasyāśvamedho bhavadbhir anubhūyatām
english: "And the kings are to be told, together with all their friends: 'Let Yudhiṣṭhira's horse-sacrifice be witnessed by you.'"

sanskrit: iti bhrātṛvacaḥ śrutvā na hanmi tvāṃ janādhipa uttiṣṭha na bhayaṃ te 'sti svastimān gaccha pārthiva
english: Having heard these words of my brother, I do not slay you, O lord of men. Rise; you have nothing to fear; go in safety, O king.

sanskrit: āgacchethā mahārāja parāṃ caitrīm upasthitām tadāśvamedho bhavitā dharmarājasya dhīmataḥ
english: Come, O great king, when the coming full moon of Caitra is at hand; then will be held the horse-sacrifice of the wise King of Righteousness.

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ sa rājā tu bhagadattātmajas tadā tathety evābravīd vākyaṃ pāṇḍavenābhinirjitaḥ
english: Thus addressed, that king, the son of Bhagadatta, then said, "So be it," vanquished as he was by the son of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca saindhavair abhavad yuddhaṃ tatas tasya kirīṭinaḥ hataśeṣair mahārāja hatānāṃ ca sutair api
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then a battle arose for the diademed one with the men of Sindhu, O great king, with those left alive from the slaughter and with the sons of the slain.

sanskrit: te 'vatīrṇam upaśrutya viṣayaṃ śvetavāhanam pratyudyayur amṛṣyanto rājānaḥ pāṇḍavarṣabham
english: Hearing that he of the white steeds had entered their realm, those kings, unable to brook it, marched out against the bull of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: aśvaṃ ca taṃ parāmṛśya viṣayānte viṣopamāḥ na bhayaṃ cakrire pārthād bhīmasenād anantarāt
english: And those men like venom, having seized that horse at the border of their realm, felt no fear of Pārtha, who came close after Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: te 'vidūrād dhanuṣpāṇiṃ yajñiyasya hayasya ca bībhatsuṃ pratyapadyanta padātinam avasthitam
english: From no great distance they came upon Bībhatsu, bow in hand, standing on foot near the sacrificial horse.

sanskrit: tatas te tu mahāvīryā rājānaḥ paryavārayan jigīṣanto naravyāghrāḥ pūrvaṃ vinikṛtā yudhi
english: Then those kings of great valor, those tigers among men, eager for victory and humiliated before in battle, surrounded him.

sanskrit: te nāmāny atha gotrāṇi karmāṇi vividhāni ca kīrtayantas tadā pārthaṃ śaravarṣair avākiran
english: Proclaiming their names, their lineages, and their manifold deeds, they then covered Pārtha with showers of arrows.

sanskrit: te kirantaḥ śarāṃs tīkṣṇān vāraṇendranivāraṇān raṇe jayam abhīpsantaḥ kaunteyaṃ paryavārayan
english: Pouring forth keen arrows able to turn back the lordliest of elephants, longing for victory in battle, they hemmed in the son of Kuntī.

sanskrit: te 'samīkṣyaiva taṃ vīram ugrakarmāṇam āhave sarve yuyudhire vīrā rathasthās taṃ padātinam
english: Without reckoning that hero of terrible deeds in war, all those heroes, mounted on their chariots, fought against him who stood on foot.

sanskrit: te tam ājaghnire vīraṃ nivātakavacāntakam saṃśaptakanihantāraṃ hantāraṃ saindhavasya ca
english: They struck at that hero, the destroyer of the Nivātakavacas, the slayer of the Saṃśaptakas and the killer of the lord of Sindhu.

sanskrit: tato rathasahasreṇa hayānām ayutena ca koṣṭhakīkṛtya kaunteyaṃ saṃprahṛṣṭam ayodhayan
english: Then with a thousand chariots and ten thousand horses they penned in the son of Kuntī as in an enclosure and, full of joy, gave him battle.

sanskrit: saṃsmaranto vadhaṃ vīrāḥ sindhurājasya dhīmataḥ jayadrathasya kauravya samare savyasācinā
english: Those heroes remembered the slaying of the wise king of Sindhu, of Jayadratha, O Kaurava, in battle by Savyasācin.

sanskrit: tataḥ parjanyavat sarve śaravṛṣṭim avāsṛjan taiḥ kīrṇaḥ śuśubhe pārtho ravir meghāntare yathā
english: Then all of them, like rain-clouds, let loose a downpour of arrows; covered by them, Pārtha shone like the sun amid the clouds.

sanskrit: sa śaraiḥ samavacchanno dadṛśe pāṇḍavarṣabhaḥ pañjarāntarasaṃcārī śakunta iva bhārata
english: Wholly veiled in arrows, that bull of the Pāṇḍavas appeared, O Bhārata, like a bird moving within a cage.

sanskrit: tato hāhākṛtaṃ sarvaṃ kaunteye śarapīḍite trailokyam abhavad rājan raviś cāsīd rajoruṇaḥ
english: Then, as the son of Kuntī was sore pressed by arrows, the whole triple world cried out in dismay, O king, and the sun grew red with dust.

sanskrit: tato vavau mahārāja māruto romaharṣaṇaḥ rāhur agrasad ādityaṃ yugapat somam eva ca
english: Then there blew, O great king, a wind that made the hair stand on end, and Rāhu swallowed the sun and the moon at one and the same time.

sanskrit: ulkāś ca jaghnire sūryaṃ vikīryantyaḥ samantataḥ vepathuś cābhavad rājan kailāsasya mahāgireḥ
english: And meteors, scattering in every direction, struck the sun, and there came a trembling, O king, upon the great mountain Kailāsa.

sanskrit: mumucuś cāsram atyuṣṇaṃ duḥkhaśokasamanvitāḥ saptarṣayo jātabhayās tathā devarṣayo 'pi ca
english: The seven seers, seized with fear, and the divine seers too, full of grief and sorrow, shed scalding tears.

sanskrit: śaśaś cāśu vinirbhidya maṇḍalaṃ śaśino 'patat viparītas tadā rājaṃs tasminn utpātalakṣaṇe
english: And the hare swiftly broke through the orb of the moon and fell, turned upside down, O king, in that portent of disaster.

sanskrit: rāsabhāruṇasaṃkāśā dhanuṣmantaḥ savidyutaḥ āvṛtya gaganaṃ meghā mumucur māṃsaśoṇitam
english: Clouds the dusky color of an ass, bearing the rainbow and the lightning, covered the sky and rained down flesh and blood.

sanskrit: evam āsīt tadā vīre śaravarṣābhisaṃvṛte loke 'smin bharataśreṣṭha tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: Such were the omens then, when the hero was enveloped in showers of arrows; in this world, O best of the Bharatas, it seemed a thing of wonder.

sanskrit: tasya tenāvakīrṇasya śarajālena sarvaśaḥ mohāt papāta gāṇḍīvam āvāpaś ca karād api
english: As he was covered on every side by that net of arrows, through a swoon the Gāṇḍīva and the quiver fell from his hand.

sanskrit: tasmin moham anuprāpte śarajālaṃ mahattaram saindhavā mumucus tūrṇaṃ gatasattve mahārathe
english: When he had fallen into that swoon, the men of Sindhu swiftly loosed a yet greater net of arrows upon the great warrior, his strength fled from him.

sanskrit: tato mohasamāpannaṃ jñātvā pārthaṃ divaukasaḥ sarve vitrastamanasas tasya śāntiparābhavan
english: Then, knowing Pārtha sunk in a swoon, all the dwellers of heaven, their minds dismayed, busied themselves to bring him back to himself.

sanskrit: tato devarṣayaḥ sarve tathā saptarṣayo 'pi ca brahmarṣayaś ca vijayaṃ jepuḥ pārthasya dhīmataḥ
english: Then all the divine seers, and the seven seers as well, and the Brahman-seers murmured prayers for the victory of the wise Pārtha.

sanskrit: tataḥ pradīpite devaiḥ pārthatejasi pārthiva tasthāv acalavad dhīmān saṃgrāme paramāstravit
english: Then, when Pārtha's energy had been kindled anew by the gods, O king, the wise master of the highest weapons stood firm as a mountain in the fight.

sanskrit: vicakarṣa dhanur divyaṃ tataḥ kauravanandanaḥ yantrasyeveha śabdo 'bhūn mahāṃs tasya punaḥ punaḥ
english: Then the joy of the Kurus drew his divine bow, and there arose from it a great sound, again and again, like that of an engine.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa śaravarṣāṇi pratyamitrān prati prabhuḥ vavarṣa dhanuṣā pārtho varṣāṇīva sureśvaraḥ
english: Then that mighty Pārtha rained down showers of arrows from his bow upon the foe, as the lord of the gods rains down his rains.

sanskrit: tatas te saindhavā yodhāḥ sarva eva sarājakāḥ nādṛśyanta śaraiḥ kīrṇāḥ śalabhair iva pāvakāḥ
english: Then all those warriors of Sindhu, kings and all, strewn over with arrows, were no longer to be seen, like fires covered with locusts.

sanskrit: tasya śabdena vitresur bhayārtāś ca vidudruvuḥ mumucuś cāśru śokārtāḥ suṣupuś cāpi saindhavāḥ
english: At the sound of his bow the men of Sindhu trembled, and tormented by fear they fled; afflicted with sorrow they shed tears, and some sank down as if asleep.

sanskrit: tāṃs tu sarvān naraśreṣṭhaḥ sarvato vicaran balī alātacakravad rājañ śarajālaiḥ samarpayat
english: And the mighty best of men, ranging on every side like a whirling circle of firebrands, O king, overwhelmed them all with nets of arrows.

sanskrit: tad indrajālapratimaṃ bāṇajālam amitrahā vyasṛjad dikṣu sarvāsu mahendra iva vajrabhṛt
english: That slayer of foes loosed in every quarter that net of shafts, like an enchantment, as the great Indra wields the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: meghajālanibhaṃ sainyaṃ vidārya sa raviprabhaḥ vibabhau kauravaśreṣṭhaḥ śaradīva divākaraḥ
english: Having rent the army that was like a mass of clouds, that best of the Kurus, radiant as the sun, shone like the maker of day in autumn.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato gāṇḍīvabhṛc chūro yuddhāya samavasthitaḥ vibabhau yudhi durdharṣo himavān acalo yathā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the heroic bearer of the Gāṇḍīva, standing ready for battle, shone unassailable in the fight like the immovable Himālaya.

sanskrit: tataḥ saindhavayodhās te punar eva vyavasthitāḥ vimuñcantaḥ susaṃrabdhāḥ śaravarṣāṇi bhārata
english: Then those warriors of Sindhu once more took their stand, and in great fury loosed their showers of arrows, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tān prasahya mahāvīryaḥ punar eva vyavasthitān tataḥ provāca kaunteyo mumūrṣūñ ślakṣṇayā girā
english: Overpowering them as they stood arrayed once more, the son of Kuntī of great valor then spoke to those bent on death in gentle words.

sanskrit: yudhyadhvaṃ parayā śaktyā yatadhvaṃ ca vadhe mama kurudhvaṃ sarvakāryāṇi mahad vo bhayam āgatam
english: "Fight with all your might, and strive to slay me; do all your tasks, for a great peril has come upon you."

sanskrit: eṣa yotsyāmi vaḥ sarvān nivārya śaravāgurām tiṣṭhadhvaṃ yuddhamanaso darpaṃ vinayitāsmi vaḥ
english: "Lo, I shall fight you all, warding off your snare of arrows; stand firm, your minds set on battle—I shall humble your pride."

sanskrit: etāvad uktvā kauravyo ruṣā gāṇḍīvabhṛt tadā tato 'tha vacanaṃ smṛtvā bhrātur jyeṣṭhasya bhārata
english: Having said this much in wrath, the Kuru bearer of the Gāṇḍīva then, O Bhārata, called to mind the words of his eldest brother.

sanskrit: na hantavyā raṇe tāta kṣatriyā vijigīṣavaḥ jetavyāś ceti yat proktaṃ dharmarājñā mahātmanā cintayām āsa ca tadā phalgunaḥ puruṣarṣabhaḥ
english: "The kṣatriyas eager for victory are not to be slain in battle, dear one, but only conquered"—so had it been told by the great-souled King of Righteousness; and Phalguna, that bull among men, then pondered upon it.

sanskrit: ity ukto 'haṃ narendreṇa na hantavyā nṛpā iti kathaṃ tan na mṛṣeha syād dharmarājavacaḥ śubham
english: "Thus was I told by the lord of men, 'The kings are not to be slain.' How may that fair word of the King of Righteousness not here be falsified?"

sanskrit: na hanyeraṃś ca rājāno rājñaś cājñā kṛtā bhavet iti saṃcintya sa tadā bhrātuḥ priyahite rataḥ provāca vākyaṃ dharmajñaḥ saindhavān yuddhadurmadān
english: "The kings should not be slain, and yet the king's command should be carried out"—so reflecting, devoted to his brother's pleasure and welfare, that knower of duty then spoke these words to the battle-maddened men of Sindhu.

sanskrit: bālān striyo vā yuṣmākaṃ na haniṣye vyavasthitān yaś ca vakṣyati saṃgrāme tavāsmīti parājitaḥ
english: "The boys and women among you who stand arrayed I shall not slay, nor him who, vanquished in the battle, shall say, 'I am yours.'"

sanskrit: etac chrutvā vaco mahyaṃ kurudhvaṃ hitam ātmanaḥ ato 'nyathā kṛcchragatā bhaviṣyatha mayārditāḥ
english: "Hearing this word of mine, do what is good for yourselves; otherwise you shall fall into distress, tormented by me."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu tān vīrān yuyudhe kurupuṃgavaḥ atvarāvān asaṃrabdhaḥ saṃrabdhair vijigīṣubhiḥ
english: Having thus spoken to those heroes, the bull of the Kurus fought on, unhurried and unangered, against those furious men bent on victory.

sanskrit: tataḥ śatasahasrāṇi śarāṇāṃ nataparvaṇām mumucuḥ saindhavā rājaṃs tadā gāṇḍīvadhanvani
english: Then the men of Sindhu loosed hundreds of thousands of arrows with smooth-jointed shafts, O king, upon the bearer of the Gāṇḍīva.

sanskrit: sa tān āpatataḥ krūrān āśīviṣaviṣopamān ciccheda niśitair bāṇair antaraiva dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Those cruel shafts, like the venom of serpents, as they flew toward him, Dhanaṃjaya cut down with his sharp arrows even in mid-course.

sanskrit: chittvā tu tān āśugamān kaṅkapatrāñ śilāśitān ekaikam eṣa daśabhir bibheda samare śaraiḥ
english: And having cut down those swift shafts, heron-feathered and whetted on stone, he pierced each man with ten arrows in the battle.

sanskrit: tataḥ prāsāṃś ca śaktīś ca punar eva dhanaṃjaye jayadrathaṃ hataṃ smṛtvā cikṣipuḥ saindhavā nṛpāḥ
english: Then, remembering the slain Jayadratha, the kings of Sindhu once more hurled javelins and lances at Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ kirīṭī saṃkalpaṃ moghaṃ cakre mahāmanāḥ sarvāṃs tān antarā chittvā mudā cukrośa pāṇḍavaḥ
english: The diademed and high-minded one made their purpose vain; cutting them all down in mid-course, the son of Pāṇḍu shouted aloud in joy.

sanskrit: tathaivāpatatāṃ teṣāṃ yodhānāṃ jayagṛddhinām śirāṃsi pātayām āsa bhallaiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ
english: And likewise, as those warriors greedy for victory rushed upon him, he struck off their heads with smooth-jointed broad-headed shafts.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ pradravatāṃ caiva punar eva ca dhāvatām nivartatāṃ ca śabdo 'bhūt pūrṇasyeva mahodadheḥ
english: And of those who fled, and ran again, and turned back once more, there arose a sound like that of the great ocean at the full.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānās tu tadā pārthenāmitatejasā yathāprāṇaṃ yathotsāhaṃ yodhayām āsur arjunam
english: Though they were being slain by Pārtha of measureless energy, they gave battle to Arjuna according to their strength and according to their zeal.

sanskrit: tatas te phalgunenājau śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ kṛtā visaṃjñā bhūyiṣṭhāḥ klāntavāhanasainikāḥ
english: Then most of them, their mounts and soldiers worn out, were robbed of their senses by Phalguna in the fight with his smooth-jointed arrows.

sanskrit: tāṃs tu sarvān pariglānān viditvā dhṛtarāṣṭrajā duḥśalā bālam ādāya naptāraṃ prayayau tadā surathasya sutaṃ vīraṃ rathenānāgasaṃ tadā
english: Knowing them all spent, Duḥśalā, daughter of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, then taking up a boy, her grandson, set out by chariot—the heroic, guiltless son of Suratha.

sanskrit: śāntyarthaṃ sarvayodhānām abhyagacchata pāṇḍavam sā dhanaṃjayam āsādya mumocārtasvaraṃ tadā dhanaṃjayo 'pi tāṃ dṛṣṭvā dhanur visasṛje prabhuḥ
english: For the sake of peace among all the warriors she approached the son of Pāṇḍu; and coming up to Dhanaṃjaya she then uttered a cry of grief, and the mighty Dhanaṃjaya, seeing her, laid down his bow.

sanskrit: samutsṛṣṭadhanuḥ pārtho vidhivad bhaginīṃ tadā prāha kiṃ karavāṇīti sā ca taṃ vākyam abravīt
english: His bow laid aside, Pārtha then duly greeted his sister and said, "What shall I do?"; and she spoke these words to him.

sanskrit: eṣa te bharataśreṣṭha svasrīyasyātmajaḥ śiśuḥ abhivādayate vīra taṃ paśya puruṣarṣabha
english: "This child, O best of the Bharatas, is the son of your sister's son; he salutes you, O hero. Behold him, O bull among men."

sanskrit: ity uktas tasya pitaraṃ sa papracchārjunas tadā kvāsāv iti tato rājan duḥśalā vākyam abravīt
english: Thus addressed, Arjuna then asked after the child's father, "Where is he?"; and thereupon, O king, Duḥśalā spoke these words.

sanskrit: pitṛśokābhisaṃtapto viṣādārto 'sya vai pitā pañcatvam agamad vīra yathā tan me nibodha ha
english: "Consumed with grief for his own father and stricken with despair, this child's father met his death, O hero; hear from me how that befell."

sanskrit: sa pūrvaṃ pitaraṃ śrutvā hataṃ yuddhe tvayānagha tvām āgataṃ ca saṃśrutya yuddhāya hayasāriṇam pituś ca mṛtyuduḥkhārto 'jahāt prāṇān dhanaṃjaya
english: "Having heard before that his father had been slain in battle by you, O sinless one, and learning that you had come, following the horse, to do battle, stricken with grief at his father's death, he gave up his life, O Dhanaṃjaya."

sanskrit: prāpto bībhatsur ity eva nāma śrutvaiva te 'nagha viṣādārtaḥ papātorvyāṃ mamāra ca mamātmajaḥ
english: "Merely on hearing your name, 'Bībhatsu has come,' O sinless one, stricken with despair my son fell to the earth and died."

sanskrit: taṃ tu dṛṣṭvā nipatitaṃ tatas tasyātmajaṃ vibho gṛhītvā samanuprāptā tvām adya śaraṇaiṣiṇī
english: "Seeing him fallen, O lord, I took up this son of his and have come to you today, seeking refuge."

sanskrit: ity uktvārtasvaraṃ sā tu mumoca dhṛtarāṣṭrajā dīnā dīnaṃ sthitaṃ pārtham abravīc cāpy adhomukham
english: Having so spoken, the daughter of Dhṛtarāṣṭra uttered a cry of grief, and, herself wretched, she addressed Pārtha, who stood downcast with his face bowed low.

sanskrit: svasāraṃ mām avekṣasva svasrīyātmajam eva ca kartum arhasi dharmajña dayāṃ mayi kurūdvaha vismṛtya kururājānaṃ taṃ ca mandaṃ jayadratham
english: "Look upon me, your sister, and upon this son of your sister's son; you should show me compassion, O knower of duty, O pride of the Kurus, forgetting the king of the Kurus and that fool Jayadratha."

sanskrit: abhimanyor yathā jātaḥ parikṣit paravīrahā tathāyaṃ surathāj jāto mama pautro mahābhuja
english: "As Parikṣit, slayer of hostile heroes, was born of Abhimanyu, so was this grandson of mine born of Suratha, O mighty-armed one."

sanskrit: tam ādāya naravyāghra saṃprāptāsmi tavāntikam śamārthaṃ sarvayodhānāṃ śṛṇu cedaṃ vaco mama
english: "Taking him up, O tiger among men, I have come into your presence for the sake of peace among all the warriors; and hear this my word."

sanskrit: āgato 'yaṃ mahābāho tasya mandasya pautrakaḥ prasādam asya bālasya tasmāt tvaṃ kartum arhasi
english: "This little grandson of that fool has come, O mighty-armed one; therefore you ought to show favor to this child."

sanskrit: eṣa prasādya śirasā mayā sārdham ariṃdama yācate tvāṃ mahābāho śamaṃ gaccha dhanaṃjaya
english: "With his head bowed in entreaty, together with me, O subduer of foes, he begs of you, O mighty-armed one: make peace, O Dhanaṃjaya."
